name: Shop
description: The missing doorway. Every piece a storefront connects to was already built -- products with prices, stock with books-aware moves, orders with lines and totals, Stripe checkout with a verified webhook, payment to invoice status to journal -- and none of it could be reached by somebody who just wanted to buy something. This package is the basket and the counter. A cart is NOT a draft order (an order is a commitment with a number and a books consequence; a basket is a browsing artefact that usually gets abandoned, and mixing them makes 'how many orders did we take?' unanswerable), it is keyed by a session token rather than an account (requiring signup before purchase is the biggest conversion loss in small-business retail), the price is stamped when a thing goes in and the DISAGREEMENT is surfaced at checkout rather than silently resolved either way, and stock is checked at checkout but moved only when money arrives -- decrementing on checkout would turn every abandoned payment into a phantom sale. The oversell race that leaves is real, documented rather than pretended away, and accepted at this scale because it surfaces at the stock move where it is visible and refundable. What makes this worth having is not the cart, which everybody has: it is that the sale posts itself. Stock moves, the invoice settles and the journal entry lands with no export, no CSV and nobody re-typing anything. Checkout now also raises that invoice and hands back the pay link in the same response: an order with no invoice gives the buyer nothing to pay, and a shopper who has just committed should not have to wait for an email to find the door. The invoice is issued 'sent', never 'draft' -- checkout IS the issuing act, and a draft would mean somebody in the back office must press a button before the person standing at the counter can hand over money. If the invoice cannot be raised the order still stands and says why; losing a sale to an invoicing hiccup is the expensive failure, and an unbilled order is visible and re-raisable. Two things a shop cannot be without now work: the basket survives leaving the page, and a product has somewhere to be read about. The basket was being minted fresh on every single visit because routed objects were never handed the request's cookies at all -- the browser sent `cart` faithfully and the platform dropped it on the floor, so the fix belongs in the server and not in this package: site objects now receive every cookie EXCEPT the identity session, which is not data but a credential, and may set exactly one response header, `set_cookie`, because a page has a real need to remember a basket and no business rewriting the server's CORS, redirect or caching posture. The product page at /shop/{product_id} is the same shop wearing a different view: full description, availability where stock is actually counted, silence where it is not, and an add form that posts to /shop like every other one, so there is one path into a basket and not two to keep in step. A withdrawn product and a mistyped id answer identically -- a friendly 404 in the same shell -- because a public page that distinguished them would be an oracle for which product ids exist. The shop now charges sales tax and postage, which it did not, and that was both a compliance problem and a straight money leak -- every parcel went out with the delivery paid by the seller. Tax and shipping are CHECKOUT MATH, not a reporting layer bolted on afterwards: retrofitting tax later means restating invoices that have already been sent to customers, which is the one repair a small business cannot make quietly. So v1 is deliberately honest rather than clever -- one flat `shop.tax_rate_bps` (0 = this shop owes none, a real answer), one `shop.tax_shipping` flag because jurisdictions genuinely disagree about whether delivery is taxable, one `shop.shipping_flat_cents` and one `shop.shipping_free_over_cents`. A flat rate admits to being a flat rate; a fake calculated one would not, and a real carrier quote needs an address, a weight and a connector that do not exist yet. The free-over threshold is in v1 rather than deferred because it is the one discount every small shop actually runs, and the page SAYS 'Free shipping' when it is earned -- a silent 0.00 reads as a shop that forgot to charge rather than one that gave the shopper something. The arithmetic lives in exactly one fold, object_cart.checkout_totals, which the order, the invoice, the preview and the basket footer all restate and none of them recompute: money added up twice is money that disagrees with itself eventually, and the disagreement always surfaces as a customer holding an invoice whose lines do not come to its total. Tax rounds half-up ONCE on the taxable base rather than per line, because tax is owed on a sale and not on each row of it -- four fifty-cent lines at 5% are 10c, not the 12c that four separately-rounded lines come to. Postage is an invoice LINE and tax is the invoice's tax_cents field: the line so a customer can see what delivery cost instead of finding it welded into a total they cannot check, and the field because invoices already have one that means exactly this, and giving the same money two homes is how totals rot. A shop that has configured none of it produces byte-identical invoices to the version before this one, because absent configuration must read as 'this shop does not do that' and never as a broken tax line.
